question.text: What happens to a call option's premium when the spot price increases (other factors constant)?

answer.text: Call premium first increases then decreases

explanation.text: The Logic: With other factors held constant, if the underlying price rises, the call option value increases (and the put option value decreases). Higher spot makes the right to buy at a fixed strike more valuable. The Trap: The opposite holds for puts: put premium decreases when spot rises, even though both are tied to the same underlying. Note: Pages 71-72 of the NISM Series-I workbook support the spot-price-versus-call/put-premium relationship used here.
